cause.draining: Codex app-server closes admission to new work during a graceful restart drain while waiting for running assistant turns and previously admitted requests. The rejected RPC says Server is draining; retry after reconnecting. NextComp previously exposed this implementation message without explaining the restart or retry behavior.
cause.ordering: Android lifecycle status changes assigned current-time activity timestamps. The list periodically promoted active/recent sessions and sorted older sessions by timestamp; completion, reconnect status changes and expiry of the thirty-second recent window could therefore reorder existing cards.
cause.limits: The observed service disconnect is consistent with a restart but does not establish which updater, signal or operator initiated it. No restart was induced in shared services.

implementation.drainingState: CODEX_DRAINING with a user-facing restart explanation and safe retry guidance, emitted as connection status without closing the existing transport. Existing completion events do not clear the draining notice. Reconnect clears the state and does not replay writes.
implementation.list: Existing seats survive lifecycle/status, timestamp churn and partial snapshots. Genuine live user messages and acknowledged phone reply requests queue replay-deduplicated ordering intent. Explicit Work taps reconcile active sessions and user-interaction batches as stable ties and intentionally scroll to the newest end. No Back, token, hydration, reconnect or idle-poll event alone is an ordering boundary. Reconciliation waits for complete results, healthy transport/admission and settled touch/scroll/tool interaction; current and archived orders remain separate.
implementation.navigation: The Work list state is retained in the parent composition across conversation selection and return; reconnect does not change the selected conversation.
implementation.meaningfulUpdates: Status badges and previews still update. Complete authoritative lists can remove archived sessions; partial discovery results retain known ongoing work.

nativeFixturePreparation.checks: Paired auth, restart status plus completing-work events, partial discovery, previews/background/new discovery, recovery/reconnect, provider/write blocking

coverage: Draining RPC preserves the original RPC error identity and exposes CODEX_DRAINING/503.
Existing completion events continue over the original connection while draining.
Reconnect clears the problem without replaying a rejected write; only explicit retry sends new work.
Status-only metadata does not manufacture recent activity.
Existing list seats survive background timestamps, active/idle changes, grace expiry and empty/partial snapshots.
New discoveries preserve existing relative order; content delivery preserves membership until a safe update.
Partial snapshots retain known sessions; complete results permit deliberate removals.
Touch/scroll hold and settle interval prevent order delivery during interaction.
Only origin-identified live started user messages create session ordering intent; hydration, tool events and completion events do not.
Explicit Work boundaries restore genuine recency and active-first stable ties; unsafe, incomplete, draining and reconnecting boundaries cannot reconcile.
Consumed interaction identities remain deduplicated across replay; unavailable session promotions remain pending.
automatedEvidence.evidenceLevel: Controlled WebSocket/RPC fixtures and Kotlin unit checks. These are not physical-phone or native gesture qualification.

nativeReviewPlan.ownership: Wait for Pocket Dev to release its existing emulator and image fixture. Do not create another emulator, restart shared services or inject work into real conversations.
nativeReviewPlan.providerInference: Blocked by construction: the fixture never connects to Codex, Firebase or a provider. Unknown operations and default accidental replies fail; a separate controlled acceptance mode acknowledges synthetic intent without executing work.
nativeReviewPlan.pairing: Synthetic token synthetic-lifecycle-only; pairing code LIFECYCLE. Configure only the explicitly granted emulator, preserving the owner's fixture preferences for restoration. Endpoint routing and app installation belong to the coordinated release owner.

scenarios.name: background-status-and-recency
scenarios.steps: Capture visible order/bounds; send background then preview; wait at least thirteen seconds; recapture.
scenarios.assert: Same visible cards retain relative order and bounds; newest preview/status becomes visible.

scenarios.name: drain-and-existing-completions
scenarios.steps: Send drain (also emits idle/status events from finishing work); inspect heading/body; wait at least thirteen seconds.
scenarios.assert: Restart meaning and safe retry instructions remain visible despite existing-work events; cards retain relative order. Banner changes viewport height, so compare keyed order separately from geometry.

scenarios.name: recovery-and-reconnect
scenarios.steps: Send recover then reconnect; wait for the automatic reconnect and list polling; recapture.
scenarios.assert: Restart notice clears; existing seats remain; fixture logs contain no unsolicited reply.

scenarios.name: partial-discovery
scenarios.steps: Scroll until a baseline card outside the partial eight-session subset is visible; send partial; wait at least thirteen seconds; send complete.
scenarios.assert: Known work never disappears during partial discovery; keyed visible anchor and relative order survive recovery.

scenarios.name: touch-and-new-discovery
scenarios.steps: Hold a pointer on a card region without activating a control; send preview/background/discover; capture during hold; release in finally; wait for safe delivery.
scenarios.assert: No card/new membership moves under the pointer; after release, new work becomes visible and latest previews arrive. Preserve a during-hold screenshot for review; do not infer the result solely from an after-release dump.

scenarios.name: scroll-and-return-anchor
scenarios.steps: Scroll away from the newest end; record a fully visible title and pixel bounds; open that card's Chat region; inject background/reconnect while detail is selected; press Back; recapture.
scenarios.assert: The selected synthetic conversation remains selected during reconnect; return restores the visible title and pixel offset.

scenarios.name: meaningful-membership
scenarios.steps: Discover a new synthetic session while idle; remove a known synthetic ID using a complete snapshot; switch Following/Working/Archived using explicit user controls.
scenarios.assert: New work and deliberate removals are delivered; existing relative order remains stable; archived order does not overwrite current order.

scenarios.name: genuine-ordering-boundaries
scenarios.steps: Emit a live user interaction for an older session while detail is selected; reconnect and return with Back. Then tap Work. Separately type and acknowledge one synthetic reply, Back, Work and reconnect.
scenarios.assert: Old activity stays in place until explicit Work; Work promotes the intended old session; Back preserves exact anchor; reconnect never resubmits the acknowledged reply.
scenarios.qualification: passed on the named candidate APK

nativeReviewPlan.publication: Reviewed synthetic native captures and bounds receipts published directly to the main gallery under nextcomp-draining-stability. Gallery validation is recorded separately below; release/physical-phone delivery belongs to Pocket Dev.

limits: The shared backend and physical phone were not changed or restarted by this workstream.
Native evidence applies to the named candidate debug APK; the coordinated signed release requires its own artifact identity/installation checks.
The native fixture acknowledges one synthetic reply but never executes real work; no inference, Firebase delivery or real-provider voice result is claimed.
Automated counts refer to the combined checkout, including concurrent Markdown image changes; no whole-release or physical-phone certification is implied.
Large-font and other physical device configurations were not requalified for this lifecycle policy.

nativeEvidence.evidenceLevel: Actual native interactions and accessibility bounds from the qualified candidate APK; synthetic data and acknowledgements. These do not establish provider inference or physical phone installation.
